notes:
Background: Vela builds a customer-facing product assistant embedded in their product dashboard. Primary users are product and support agents; latency directly impacts conversion and NPS. They migrated to a different LLM API last year but have seen intermittent latency regressions over last 2 quarters and are now evaluating alternatives.

Key ask: Hosted API trial to validate streaming first-byte latency and tool-calling end-to-end SLOs; if numbers hold, move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and VPC-only network.

Recent activity (timeline):
- 2026-01-19: Initial intro call (Ethan). Product + infra overview. AE notes: interested in streaming + function-calling.
- 2026-02-02: Technical discovery with Maya (SE) + infra (internal network team). Discussed VPC requirements, KMS.
- 2026-02-11: POC kickoff (Fireflies ff_2026-02-11_7564). Agreed scope: 2-week POC using Hosted API + benchmark harness (simulated agent sessions, 50-200 concurrent users).
- 2026-02-24: Run benchmarks comparing Redwood streaming vs incumbent provider (internal harness). Collected first-byte/streaming-start, token-to-token, function-call latency. (drive:1Vela-POC-Benchmarks)
- 2026-03-03: Review call with product and infra; POC logs shared. Follow-up pricing ask for Dedicated.

POC / Benchmark summary (high-level):
- Workload: conversational agent with tool-calling to product search and billing APIs. Mixed prompt lengths (avg 150 tokens), streaming-first required. Target SLO: median first-byte < 300ms, p95 < 700ms, function-call end-to-end < 800ms. Cost sensitivity: mid (will trade some $ for stable latency).
- Redwood Hosted results (observed during POC): median first-byte ~ 95-140ms, p95 first-byte ~ 280-360ms, token-to-token steady ~15-30ms, end-to-end function-call (invoke + response stream) median ~120ms, p95 ~380ms. Observed stable streaming chunks and low jitter.
- Incumbent provider results (customer-side baseline): median first-byte ~ 320-450ms (varies across runs), p95 first-byte often > 1s during regressions, token-to-token bursts and higher jitter, function-call E2E median ~420ms but with 95th > 1.2s in degraded windows.
- Notes: Incumbent regressions correlated with concurrent background batch jobs on their side (per customer support notes) but root cause not shared. Vela engineering: "We see UX stutters — unacceptable for customer-facing agent."

Operational asks surfaced by Vela:
- Clear SLA for streaming start latency and token tail latency (p95/p99).
- Ability to pin model versions and fallback policies for Dedicated.
- KMS integration and audit logs for calls.
- Pricing comparison: Hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved GPUs (they want a modeled run-rate for 6/12 month commit).

Sales/Commercial notes:
- Vela is willing to pilot Dedicated if Redwood can provide a 90-day reserved capacity trial window or conservative pricing demo. Procurement wants a line-item comparison (incumbent vs Redwood) and a 2nd reference.
- Estimated ARR if move to Dedicated and roll out across product support & onboarding is ~$120k/year (conservative) — matches their forecast ask.

Quotes / snippets from calls:
- Product lead: "We can't ship an assistant that pauses mid-sentence — it destroys trust."
- Infra lead: "If Redwood's streaming numbers are repeatable we'll consider moving to Dedicated behind our VPC."
- AE note: "Strong technical interest. Main decision hinge is latency stability and clear migration path."

Next steps (action items):
1) Ethan to schedule pricing + SLA call with Vela procurement (week of 2026-03-08).
2) Maya to provide Dedicated capacity sketch and 90-day trial proposal.
3) SE follow-up: deliver trimmed benchmark deck with plots (first-byte distributions, p95/p99 comparisons) and sample tracing spans.
4) Security: share SOC2 report + KMS integration patterns (drive:vela-dedicated-pricing-deck).

CRM shorthand / quick wins:
- Push dedicated trial offer + reference intro to similar mid-market customer.
- Highlight streaming start benchmarks and tool-calling latency in the deck.
- Confirm VPC network checklist early to unblock procurement.
